- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates price spikes in the 30-day horizon — especially after strong sentiment shifts — apply a 5–10% upward bias to spike periods.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if price deviates >10% from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average with smoothing.  
- In low-sentiment environments, model tends to forecast lower than true outcome — apply a “sentiment-adjusted floor” to prevent deep bearish underestimation.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overpredicts early in the horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) — reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% to reflect slower momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows recent reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often misses the turn — increase forecast slope to reflect momentum shift.
